title: Torsion bound for supported finite images and actual integral image reductions
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites in the small indexing universe [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. A support chain over $X$ means a finite chain $S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0=X$, where each arrow is a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a condensed coefficient ring $R$, put $R_T=p_T^*R$ and $\mathcal A_{R,T}=\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}$. Write $J_R=J_{R,1}\circ\cdots\circ J_{R,r}$, where $J_{R,t}=(a_t)_!$ in the open case and $J_{R,t}=(a_t)_*$ in the closed case [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. For an affine pro-étale object $v:U\to X$, set $F_{R,v}=v^*J_R$. The empty chain has $J_R=\mathrm{id}$. All derived categories and $R\Gamma$ are the ordinary uncompleted module-derived ones, with section complexes valued in abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Fix a prime $\ell$ and an integer $d\geq0$. Assume that $H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},G)=0$ for every affine étale $V\to X$, every locally torsion abelian sheaf $G$ on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $q>d$, with no common annihilator required [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

A finite scalar local model means a module which on a pro-étale cover has the form $R_T\otimes_{\underline{R(*)}}\underline P$, where $P$ is a finitely presented scalar $R(*)$-module, that is, a cokernel of a map between finite free scalar modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The scalar modules and covers may differ for different terms. For any actual module map $f:L\to M$ between such modules on $S$, write $I_f=\operatorname{im}f$ in the abelian module category, not the closure of a topological image.

For every finite commutative discrete ring $R=A$ killed by a power of $\ell$ [sk-def-localizing-closure], every support chain, every map $f$ as above, every affine pro-étale $v$, and every $q>d$,
$$H^qR\Gamma(U,F_{A,v}(I_f)[0])=0.$$
For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $B=\mathcal O_E$ with its norm topology and let $\pi$ be a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $B_T=p_T^*C(-,B)$ and $k_{n,T}=(B/\pi^n)_T$, with the finite discrete coefficients, for $n\geq1$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ gives $B=\mathbf Z_\ell$. For $R=C(-,B)$ and an integral map $f$ as above, put $K_f=F_{B,v}(I_f)[0]$ and form its actual derived reductions, restricted back to $B_U$-modules,
$$K_{f,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{B_U\to k_{n,U}}(K_f\otimes^L_{B_U}k_{n,U}).$$
Then for every $n\geq1$ and $q>d$,
$$H^qR\Gamma(U,K_{f,n})=0.$$
The second assertion is about reductions of the actual supported image, not images of the reduced map. It asserts neither completeness nor an integral bound, and does not assume that these reductions have classical cohomology. All chains, maps, affine objects, zero rings and empty schemes are allowed.

source.place: Section 8, condition (8.1), proof of Lemma 8.6, torsion paragraph; Bhatt--Scholze Corollary 5.1.6 and Stacks Tag 099W, proetale.tex lemma-compare-cohomology, for classical inputs only. Agent torsion-reduction obligation; the arbitrary supported image reduction assertion without a classicality hypothesis is WANTED, not asserted to follow from that comparison alone.

proof.text: For the finite coefficient conjunct, introduce A and the given local models and apply supported_finite_image_cohomology_vanishes. The prime-power annihilator is unnecessary for that stronger theorem.

For the integral conjunct, let K=(v^*J(image f))[0]. The first-power bound is precisely supported_image_first_reduction_cohomology_vanishes. Retain its explicit dispute: no use is made of the refuted unrestricted relative-comparison lemma.

Use principal_tensor_scalar_extension to identify each canonical restricted level n with tensor reduction at positive exponent n+1. The coefficient resolution theorem gives the distinguished triangle K_1 -> K_(m+2) -> K_(m+1) -> K_1[1] for every m>=0. This holds for arbitrary K and needs neither flatness nor completeness.

Fix q>d and put H=H^q R(condensedModuleSections B U). The right-derived functor is triangulated and homology is homological, so H maps each coefficient triangle to an exact three-term sequence. The first-power term is zero. Induction on m, starting at exponent one, makes the third term zero, hence the middle term zero. Transport along the tensor/scalar-extension isomorphism to get the canonical restricted reduction at every level. Pair this integral result with the finite result. This is real coefficient-power induction; the remaining first-power geometric bound is an explicit smaller unresolved obligation.

proof_origin.place: Triangles paragraph: coefficient-power induction after the first reduction, plus the existing finite coefficient bound. First-power geometric vanishing is isolated with the inherited Q09 dispute; net hole count is unchanged.
